root_cause.text: In `net/rds/rdma.c::__rds_rdma_map()`, the `put_user()` failure path incorrectly freed/unpinned `pages` and `sg` after `get_mr()` had already transferred ownership of those resources to the transport/MR, causing a double cleanup when the MR reference was later released.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly says "`__rds_rdma_map()` hands sg/pages ownership to the transport after `get_mr()` succeeds" and that on cookie copy failure "the error path must not free those resources again"; the patch removes `unpin_user_pages(pages, nr_pages);` and `kfree(sg);` from the `put_user()` error branch so cleanup happens only through the final MR teardown path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove redundant cleanup on the put_user failure path so resources are released consistently through the shared exit path.
intent_record.what: The change removes a conditional cleanup block inside the put_user(cookie, ...) failure path in __rds_rdma_map(), specifically deleting the calls to unpin_user_pages(pages, nr_pages) and kfree(sg) when !need_odp before setting ret = -EFAULT and jumping to out.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when writing the cookie back to userspace fails, the function no longer performs this immediate manual cleanup in that branch and instead relies on the common out path for resource handling. This prevents duplicate or inconsistent freeing/unpinning of pages and scatter-gather memory on that error path.

grouping_result.intent: Remove redundant cleanup on the put_user failure path so resources are released consistently through the shared exit path.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it removes the erroneous extra cleanup on the put_user() failure path after ownership had already been transferred by get_mr(), preventing double free/unpin via the later MR release path.

candidates.rationale: On the put_user() failure path, this explicitly unpinned pages after get_mr() had already taken ownership of them, leading to a double cleanup when the MR was later released.
This freed the scatterlist on the put_user() failure path even though ownership had already been transferred to the MR/transport by get_mr(), causing a second release later.

vuln_statements.explanation: After get_mr() had already transferred ownership of the pinned pages to the MR/transport, this put_user() failure-path cleanup unpinned them again, causing double cleanup when the MR was later released.
After get_mr() had already transferred ownership of the scatterlist to the MR/transport, this put_user() failure-path cleanup freed it prematurely, leading to a second free during later MR release.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown body of __rds_rdma_map() is sufficient because it includes the exact put_user() failure path and the cleanup logic after MR creation. The vulnerable construct is present. After the transport get_mr() succeeds, ownership is described as transferred: the earlier error path comments that on success the transport owns the pages/sg and only on failure 'we need to release anything.' Yet later, in the put_user() failure path, the code does: 'if (args->cookie_addr && put_user(cookie, ...)) { if (!need_odp) { unpin_user_pages(pages, nr_pages); kfree(sg); } ret = -EFAULT; goto out; }'. This means pages and sg are explicitly freed/unpinned after get_mr() has already succeeded and ownership has been handed off to the transport/MR, matching the stated root cause of double cleanup when the MR is later released. Therefore has_bug=true. The fix is not present here because the erroneous cleanup still happens in the put_user() failure block; a fixed version would avoid unpinning/freeing pages/sg after successful get_mr() ownership transfer. Hence is_fixed=false.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable logic is fully visible in `__rds_rdma_map()`. After pinning pages and building `sg`, the code calls `trans_private = rs->rs_transport->get_mr(sg, nents, rs, &mr->r_key);` and explicitly documents ownership transfer: `/* Obtain a transport specific MR. If this succeeds, the s/g list is now owned by the MR. */`. On success it stores `mr->r_trans_private = trans_private;`. However, if the later `put_user()` fails — `if (args->cookie_addr && put_user(cookie, ...)) { ret = -EFAULT; goto out; }` — execution goes to the common `out:` path, which does `if (mr) rds_mr_put(mr);`. Releasing the MR will eventually invoke `rds_destroy_mr()`, which calls `mr->r_trans->free_mr(trans_private, mr->r_invalidate);`, i.e. transport-side cleanup of the resources now owned by the MR. This is exactly the vulnerable condition described: after `get_mr()` has transferred ownership to the MR/transport, the `put_user()` failure path still tears down the MR via `rds_mr_put(mr)`, causing cleanup of resources that were already handed off. There is no special handling to avoid this post-`get_mr()` cleanup on `put_user()` failure, so the fix is not present.

After pinning pages and building the scatterlist, the code calls `trans_private = rs->rs_transport->get_mr(sg, nents, rs, &mr->r_key);` and explicitly documents ownership transfer: `/* Obtain a transport specific MR.
